summary: Staged attenuation and snapshot rehydrate guidance for tenant suffering cost/throughput spike after combined batching+prefetch+quant change
description: Issue summary: LuminaHealth reported a sudden per-token cost increase (~3x) and elevated 5xx rates for a specific tenant after enabling a combined optimization bundle (dynamic batching bump, aggressive KV prefetch, int8 quant profile). Impact: production traffic for LuminaHealth faced degraded tail latency, increased cost, and user-visible errors for ~15% of sessions. Environment: Dedicated capacity, prod-us-east, tenant id TLN-998. First observed: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC. Customer timeframe: they enabled the optimizer bundle via Console feature flags during a morning deployment window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated tenant using redwood/open-7b-int8-v2, enable: (a) dynamic_batching.max_batch_size=2048 (b) kv_prefetch.enabled=true (c) quant_profile=aggressive-int8-v2. 2) Ramp traffic to steady QPS similar to LuminaHealth (~1.8x baseline). 3) Observe a spike in per-token CPU/GPU churn, KV eviction spikes, and increased 5xx/timeouts. Note: issue reproduces within 10-20 minutes for this workload distribution.
observed_logs_and_metrics: - spikes in serving-runtime OOM-ish evictions: eviction_rate tenant TLN-998 +420% at 09:19 UTC. - tail latency (95/99p) rose from 160ms/320ms to 480ms/1.9s. - backend 5xx rate increased from 0.2% to 3.7% for the tenant. - KV cache miss ratio jumped when prefetch collided with async evictions. - Billing spike: estimated per-token compute cost x2.9 for the affected window. Relevant logs: /logs/prod/us-east/serving/TLN-998/2026-03-10-09*.gz
customer_reproduction_attempts: Customer rolled the toggle back once but re-applied the optimizer bundle with a slightly higher batch size; reported inconsistent results. They captured a short recording and A/B traffic split showing the degradation tied to the combined flags rather than any single change.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: interaction between aggressive batching, int8 execution path, and KV prefetch created contention for memory and CPU/GPU transfer resources leading to eviction churn and excessive kernel fallback. Checks performed: - Confirmed tenant-specific snapshot of optimizer flags via Console. - Queried runtime traces: saw frequent kernel re-selection for int8 paths and repeated KV cache eviction events. - Checked autoscaler: no global shortage but per-gpu memory pressure for tenant-scheduled pods. - Confirmed no infra-level network errors in the window. Correlation: pattern matches previous incidents where mixed aggressive quant + prefetch caused oscillation (see linked SUP-96122).
temporary_mitigation_applied: 1) Applied immediate per-tenant throttling: rate cap lowered by 30% for TLN-998 at 09:34 UTC. 2) Forced routing to fallback model variant redwood/open-7b-fp16 for the tenant at 09:40 UTC. 3) Disabled kv_prefetch for the tenant at 09:42 UTC. 4) Snapshot restore: rehydrated last known-good optimizer snapshot (2026-03-09) to ensure baseline flags. Effects: 5xx rate reduced back toward baseline within 8 minutes; tail latency normalized after model fallback and kv_prefetch disable.
root_cause_hypothesis: The primary cause appears to be a resource contention feedback loop: aggressive batching increased per-request resource footprint on the int8 path; concurrent KV prefetch increased memory pressure and eviction churn; the runtime's kernel selection fell back intermittently causing amplification in latency and compute. The combination produced a cost/throughput regression not seen when any single optimization was enabled alone.
resolution: Resolved for the immediate incident by: (a) enforcing temporary tenant throttles, (b) switching tenant traffic to fp16 variant, (c) disabling kv_prefetch, and (d) restoring last-known-good optimizer snapshot. Customer confirmed service returned to acceptable latency and cost profile by 2026-03-10 09:53 UTC. Status: mitigated, monitoring for recurrence.
long_term_recommendations: 1) Add per-tenant safety gates that prevent enabling aggressive quant + kv_prefetch + high batch_size simultaneously without staged rollouts. 2) Implement a runtime circuit-breaker metric (combined memory-eviction + kernel-fallback) to auto-demote to conservative profile. 3) Create a Console preflight check that simulates resource impact for a tenant using representative traffic. 4) Update docs with explicit matrix of compatible optimizer flags and recommended staging steps. 5) Schedule a follow-up E2E test with LuminaHealth traffic patterns in staging.
follow_up_tasks: Run staging replay for LuminaHealth workload 2026-03-15
resolution_notes: Customer notified of mitigations and agreed to staged re-test under Support supervision. Engineering to own follow-up tasks; Support will keep the ticket open until the automation and gating are in place and tested with the customer.
